question: The income of Raman is ₹83,000. He saves 16% of his income. If his income increases by 22% and expenditure increases by 25%, then his savings will:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial saving = 16% of 83000 = 13280

Expenditure = 84% of 83000 = 69720

New income = 83000 × 1.22 = 101260

New expenditure = 69720 × 1.25 = 87150

New saving = 101260 − 87150 = 14110

Increase = 14110 − 13280 = 830

**∴ Answer = ₹830**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Income = 83000, Saving = 16%

Income increases by 22%, Expenditure increases by 25%

**Formula used:**

Saving = Income − Expenditure

**Calculation:**

⇒ Initial saving = 0.16 × 83000 = 13280

⇒ Initial expenditure = 83000 − 13280 = 69720

⇒ New income = 83000 × 1.22 = 101260

⇒ New expenditure = 69720 × 1.25 = 87150

⇒ New saving = 101260 − 87150 = 14110

⇒ Increase in saving = 14110 − 13280 = 830

**∴ The correct answer is ₹830.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Saving Concept

Saving = Income − Expenditure

Percentage Change

New value = Old × (1 + percentage change)

Expenditure Relation

If saving is 16%, expenditure is 84% of income

Practical Insight

Savings increase only if income grows faster than expenditure

1b
